answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation climb a one-way ladder: every identity starts at the base and rises only by finishing useful work that established agents endorse, with each rung demanding a bridge of endorsements from a higher rung than the last. A fake army stalls at the bottom because its own endorsements carry no weight, so the attacker must do real sequential work for every copy, like weaving velvet one thread at a time on a reef of shared trust rather than stamping out copies in bulk. The cost grows with each identity and cannot be bought in bulk.
